'''''Heliconia latispatha''''' ('''expanded lobsterclaw''')<ref>{{PLANTS|id=HELA12|taxon=Heliconia latispatha|accessdate=14 May 2015}}</ref> is a plant species native to southern [[Mexico]] ([[Tabasco]], [[Oaxaca]], [[Chiapas]], [[Campeche]]), [[Central America]] and northern [[South America]] ([[Colombia]], [[Venezuela]], [[Ecuador]] and [[Peru]]) and naturalized in [[Florida]] and [[Jamaica]].<ref name="evangelinatelloalvarez">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=248454 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Heliconia latispatha'' ]</ref> It is an [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] up to 4 m tall, with leaves resembling those of [[bananas]]. The [[inflorescence]] is erect, up to 45 cm long, with red or orange bracts subtending green, yellow or orange flowers.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=222000082 Flora of North America v 22, ''Heliconia latispatha'' ]</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/780360#page/221/mode/1up George Bentham. 1846. Botany of the Voyage of H.M.S. Sulphur 170–171, ''Heliconia latispatha ''].</ref>
